a2-unit-45.45.1 Welcome to the studio:
Manager: Good morning, everybody! Can I have your attention, please? This is Jordan, our new intern. He's starting with us today for a six-month internship. Jordan, let me show you what we do. As you probably know, the first stage in making a video game is planning. At the planning stage, the budget is agreed, and the target audience is chosen. Nora, tell Jordan about it.
Nora: Hi Jordan! Before we agree on the budget and choose the target audience, we come up with an original idea for a game. I love creating fantasy games. That's my favorite genre! Right now, I'm writing a story for a game called Castle Dreams, and Annie is producing some basic artwork for the characters. After the artwork is produced, we work with the engineers to create a prototype. That's the first working version of the game.
Manager: Thanks, Nora. Over here is the production team. They design the levels and write the code. At this stage, the character models are created, and the voices and sound effects are recorded. Marlon creates the models, and Eloise records the sound effects.
Manager: When everything is ready, the game is tested by lots of people. Remi's team tests the game to make sure everything works. They look for bugs, which are mistakes in the code. When they find a bug, they fix the code. I think testing is the most difficult stage. Sometimes new bugs are found months after the game goes on sale!
Manager: And that brings us to the launch stage. Natasha is the team leader, but she's at a video game event today. Her team promotes the game. They plan the advertising and make videos of people playing the game. After the videos are made, they're put on social media.
Manager: Jordan, you told me you play our games every weekend, right? So, do you have any questions?
